notes: 10-K narrative is unusually generic re: named DoD programs. Filing references Gotham as defense/intel platform but does NOT cite PE numbers, Project Maven, TITAN, MetaConstellation by name (the latter three are cohort-metadata named programs). Forward narrative leans on aggregate U.S. Government revenue concentration, IDIQ ceiling ($12.3B), and government remaining-deal-value ($4.4B). Claims below mix (a) the cohort-flagged named programs (testable against pentagon_jbook even though filing names them only via product framing) and (b) filing-grounded aggregate claims.

claims.claim_text: Gotham powers a wide array of allied defense and intelligence missions and has surfaced insights for global defense agencies and the intelligence community 'for over a decade' (i.e., a durable, growing prime DoD/IC franchise).
claims.subject: Palantir Gotham
claims.object_value: ongoing prime franchise across DoD + IC + allied defense
claims.source_quote: Gotham integrates with our other platforms, as well as our broader defense offerings, to power a wide array of missions across allied defense and intelligence operations. For over a decade, Gotham has surfaced insights for global defense agencies, the intelligence community, disaster relief organizations and beyond.

claims.claim_text: Cohort-metadata flagged: Palantir is the prime / key software provider on Project Maven (Army intel/AI). The 10-K's defense/intel narrative (Gotham + AIP for 'special forces personnel and military officials') is implicitly reliant on Maven-class programs of record.
claims.subject: Project Maven
claims.object_value: Maven Smart System / Army intel AI
claims.source_quote: (implied) 'special forces personnel and military officials in the United States and abroad' and 'our broader defense offerings'; the filing does not name Maven explicitly but the cohort metadata flags it as a material PLTR program.

claims.claim_text: Cohort-metadata flagged: Palantir is the prime on TITAN (Army Tactical Intelligence Targeting Access Node). TITAN is an Army program-of-record awarded to Palantir in 2024 and is a load-bearing forward-revenue narrative for the DoD segment.
claims.subject: TITAN (Tactical Intelligence Targeting Access Node)
claims.object_value: Army RDT&E / Procurement line items for TITAN ground stations
claims.source_quote: (implied) '$12.3 billion of IDIQ contracts ... where the funding of such contracts has not yet been determined or guaranteed'; cohort metadata flags TITAN as a named PLTR program.

claims.claim_text: Cohort-metadata flagged: MetaConstellation is a named Palantir defense product (multi-satellite tasking) that has been pitched as a forward growth vector for the IC / Space Force / commercial space community.
claims.subject: MetaConstellation
claims.object_value: tasking software for proliferated LEO constellations
claims.source_quote: (implied) 'industries such as airline, space, shipbuilding ... and government' and 'broader defense offerings'; cohort metadata flags MetaConstellation by name.

claims.claim_text: Government segment generated 54% of $4.5B in 2025 revenue (~$2.43B), with US share at 74% of total. Forward government contract remaining deal value was $4.4B (up 90% YoY); IDIQ contract ceiling stood at an unfunded $12.3B.
claims.subject: PLTR government segment
claims.object_value: $2.43B FY25 gov revenue; $4.4B remaining gov deal value; $12.3B IDIQ ceiling unfunded
claims.source_quote: Of the $4.5 billion in revenue that we generated in 2025, 54% came from customers in the government segment, and 46% came from customers in the commercial segment ... the total remaining deal value of the contracts that we had been awarded by government agencies ... was $4.4 billion, up 90% from December 31, 2024 ... we do not include government contracts known as IDIQ contracts, totaling $12.3 billion, as of December 31, 2025, that we have also been awarded, but where the funding of such contracts has not yet been determined or guaranteed.

claims.claim_text: Palantir asserts it is uniquely positioned to capture an even greater share of U.S. federal government spending on software systems going forward (i.e., the forward thesis depends on DoD/IC software-procurement budget growth).
claims.subject: PLTR forward thesis
claims.object_value: growing share of US federal software spend
claims.source_quote: We continue to believe we are uniquely positioned to provide commercially available software to the U.S. federal government. Our government customers remain a meaningful source of revenue for our business. We intend to capture an even greater share of U.S. federal government spending on software systems.

claims.claim_text: Control claim (non-J-Book): Palantir leases principal properties in Denver, Palo Alto, NYC, Washington DC, and London.
claims.subject: PLTR facilities
claims.object_value: Denver, Palo Alto, NYC, DC, London
claims.source_quote: We have leased principal properties in Denver, Colorado, which was the location of our corporate headquarters; in Palo Alto, California; New York City, New York; Washington, D.C.; and London, England.

claims.claim_text: Control claim (non-J-Book): Palantir is committed to spending at least $1.95B over ten contract years through Sept 30, 2033 with one third-party cloud services provider; satisfied $79.2M of $170.2M for the year beginning Oct 1, 2025.
claims.subject: PLTR cloud commitment
claims.source_quote: the Company has committed to spend at least $ 1.95 billion over ten contract years through September 30, 2033 ... the Company satisfied $ 79.2 million of its $ 170.2 million commitment for the contract year beginning October 1, 2025 and ending September 30, 2026.
